task: Translate the recommended Starlight character territory into an original live-action cinematic system, then redesign five characters so costume, silhouette, instrument, gesture, limit, and ensemble action express one coherent responsibility.
surface: Internal character direction, costume development, cinematic keyframes, and future North Star production guidance
audience: Starlight founder, character designers, costume and production designers, prompt operators, runtime owners, and independent visual reviewers
first_read: Five beautiful, unmistakably different civic operators form one material civilization while making routing, comparison, welcome, provenance, interpretation, limits, and handoffs physically legible.

keep: Contemporary near-future architectural tailoring with tactile human fabrics
Separate inspectable instruments that reveal transformation, stop, rollback, and handoff
Role-readable silhouettes, body types, age ranges, gestures, and material allocations
Limestone, pale wood, woven acoustic surfaces, glass, steel, daylight, and restrained practical light
Charcoal, warm bone, graphite, mineral gray, plum, muted clay, oxblood, and sparse oxidized red
avoid: Marvel or named-artist imitation, franchise characters, copied costumes, logos, or trade dress
Superhero posing, chest emblems, capes, masks, spandex, powered armor, tactical gear, and militarism
Steampunk, Victorian, fantasy, cosmic, robot, black-glass, cyan-gold, and unmotivated glow defaults
Generated exact text, labels, diagrams, evidence, logos, watermarks, or interface copy
A fleet uniform that collapses role, body, motion, and instrument distinction
direction.signature: Bounded intelligence becomes cinematic when a responsible person uses a separable, inspectable instrument to make a consequential decision and handoff visible.
system: Person equals responsibility, judgment, limit, and relationship
Instrument equals transformation, evidence, handoff, and state
Cinema equals consequence made visible through performance, material, space, lens, and motivated light
Practical fabrication and actor mobility precede speculative finish
One identity anchor followed by bounded batches and collision scenes

The v3 character board and v3 ensemble form the promoted direction; earlier versions remain diagnostic provenance.

checks.name: costume-continuity
checks.evidence: The same five identities, faces, role order, distinct v3 costumes, individual color families, silhouettes, and exclusive instruments remain legible from the v3 board into the v3 ensemble proof.

checks.name: story-and-role-readability
checks.evidence: Orchestrator rotates one route open, Sentinel overlaps two lenses to expose a mismatch, Concierge opens one aperture, Weaver keeps incoming strands separate through an open braid, and Starlight Sage fans nested leaves while returning an incomplete judgment. The ensemble makes their causal handoff visible without labels.

checks.name: text-and-casing
checks.evidence: No title, interface copy, logo, label, or all-caps designed text is present in the promoted v3 assets. Evidence surfaces are blank or use simple abstract nonlinguistic lines and nodes; future exact notation remains deterministic.

checks.name: rights-and-originality
checks.evidence: The final assets contain no Marvel character, copied costume, logo, trade dress, named-artist imitation, or recognizable franchise expression. The design uses original Starlight roles, mechanisms, palette, architecture, and bounded-intelligence thesis.

score.notes: Ships as an internal cinematic direction proof and production-development package. It is not character canon or a public campaign master; founder territory approval, G0 roster truth, full turnarounds, deterministic notation, broader continuity tests, and the 95-point release receipt remain mandatory.

known_risks: Only five of the 13 North Stars are represented; the remaining eight could still expose silhouette, palette, or instrument-family collisions.
The promoted ensemble needs a second action, deeper spatial blocking, partial occlusion, and mobile-crop continuity test; any future exact notation must still be applied deterministically.
Ensemble v1 is preserved only as iteration provenance and must not be promoted because it contains nonsemantic background marks.
The earlier Orchestrator solo keyframe is visually superseded; a v3 solo performance frame and full turnaround remain required.
A single face and costume view cannot prove identity continuity across profile, back, seated, motion, pressure, weather, or alternate lighting states.
The tools are visually plausible but require ergonomic, folding, balance, safety, and fabrication mockups before production claims.
Generated fictional performers are character-development references, not a grant of real-person casting, likeness, union, or publicity rights.
Founder representation selection, Queen and Orchestrator identity resolution, and G0 roster crosswalk remain open; these assets do not bypass those gates.
